story: The illustrative Noise ID feature gets a large MDI share but almost no held-out permutation share. Select a feature and compare its two scores; changing the ranking method exposes how differently the methods order the same features.

aha.observation: Noise ID ranks first on MDI with a 45% share, but last on held-out permutation with a 1% share. These are normalized method shares, not raw accuracy drops.

data.title: Noise can look important.
data.heading: Illustrative normalized feature importance
data.prompt: compare impurity-based feature importance with permutation importance when one feature is random noise
data.instructions: Inspect Noise ID. Compare its values and ranks under the two methods.
calculations: The supplied illustrative arrays are MDI [35,20,45] and held-out permutation [75,24,1] for x, y and Noise ID.
Each series is normalized to 100%; no raw permutation accuracy drops or Noise ID training rows were supplied.
Ranks are computed by descending score, with stable source order for ties. Noise ID has rank 1 under MDI and rank 3 under permutation.
Totals are sums of the supplied shares. Reordering never changes values or denominators.
data.sourceKind: illustrative normalized shares, not the eight-row toy forest
